t:
In this Act:
    (1) National fire danger rating system.—The term “national fire danger rating system” means the national system used to provide a measure of fire danger according to a range of low to moderate to high to very high to extreme. 
    (2) Prescribed burn.—The term “prescribed burn” means a planned fire intentionally ignited. 
    (3) Secretary.—The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture, acting through the Chief of the Forest Service.

fable.w: This section only defines terms (national fire danger rating system, prescribed burn, Secretary) and creates no process for consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, or suits involving anyone outside the federal government. The only actors named are federal officials, so the tempting reading that a 'national system' or prescribed-burn context implies state or public coordination fails; nothing in the text requires or authorizes outside involvement in a federal decision.
fable.s: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture, acting through the Chief of the Forest Service.

**Step 1: The tempting reading.** The section mentions a "national fire danger rating system" and defines "Secretary," which might suggest some federal decision process. It doesn't qualify, because this is only a definitions section. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue, and it involves no party outside the federal government.
